idea_headline: A front page, not a web page.
idea: Broadsheet sets a feature the way a newspaper would: a blackletter masthead between rules, a bold serif headline with one red word, an italic deck, body in columns with a drop cap, engraved plates for pictures, and figures pulled into the margin. The reader gets a document that feels reported.
use_for: Features and long reads, pilot reports, newsletters and digests, anything that benefits from the authority of print and the rhythm of columns.
avoid_when: Interactive tools, dashboards, anything scanned rather than read, or subjects that need colour to carry meaning.
principles: The masthead is the only ornament.
Blackletter appears once, centred, between a double rule. Everywhere else, Old Standard and Franklin do the work.
Body text runs in two or three columns above 760px, with hairline rules between. Pull figures and plates break the columns; nothing else does.
The red is a single word in the headline, a pull figure, or a link. It is never a block, never a background larger than a tint box.
Pictures are engravings: hatched line drawings in ink, framed, captioned with a Fig. number. Mark invented scenes as illustrative.
Every percentage names its base in the same sentence: 26 of 42 respondents. Transactions are not shoppers; the small print says so.
voice: Reported, past tense, specific: "The pilot opened at 5 a.m. for six Sundays."
Crossheads are claims, set in bold serif.
Invented voices are labelled illustrative in the small print, never presented as interviews.
colour_note: Day is newsprint: warm off-white, black ink, hairline rules, one red. Night is the night edition: a near-black warm ground, cream ink, the red lifted. Status colours live in ledgers only; on the page, red is the only colour.
chart_note: Charts are printed in ink with the exception in red. Hatching or a lighter ink separates series; never a third hue. Direct labels in Franklin caps; no legend boxes.
type_headline: UnifrakturCook once; Old Standard, Franklin and Courier for the rest.
type_note: Four families. The blackletter masthead appears once. Old Standard TT carries headlines, decks and body. Libre Franklin in caps carries the apparatus. Courier Prime carries wire copy and tables of figures.
space_headline: Column rules, double rules, a drop cap.
space: Body column width; two or three columns above 760px with 24px gutters.
Between a rule and the text under it.
edges: Everything. Newsprint is cut, not rounded.
A 2px ink rule over a 1px rule: under the masthead, above the folio.
Around every engraving, with the caption outside.
depth: The first letter of the piece, three lines deep, in Old Standard bold.
None by default. Reveal is a page turn: content is simply there. Plates may draw in (stroke) on first view; reduced motion shows them complete.
components_headline: Boxes, plates, pull figures, the ledger.
components_note: Kit components take Broadsheet through the contract: newsprint grounds, red primary, zero radius, hairline borders. Authored classes add the rules, the plate frame, the pull figure and the drop cap.

callouts_note: Callouts are boxed notes with a bold lead word, in the body face. Caveats take caution; the decision takes the red rule.
chart_comp_note: Charts are ink with one red exception, labelled directly. Title the figure with a Fig. number in Franklin caps.
table_note: Tables are the record: Courier figures, hairline rows, Franklin caps headers. Status is a word in the last column.
card_note: A card is a plate: an engraving in a 1px frame with a Fig. caption below in Franklin caps. The engraving is hatched ink, never a photograph.
motifs_headline: Mastheads, plates, pull figures, box scores, jump lines.
motifs_note: Broadsheet draws with the furniture of a front page. The data lives in pull figures, in box scores and in engraved plates whose details are the counts: one specimen per unit of the sample.

motifs.title: The jump line and the folio
motifs.usage: "Continued on page 4" in Franklin caps closes a column that breaks; the folio (name · page) sits above the bottom double rule. They tell the reader the page has an edge.

sample_note: A front page opener: masthead and rules, the headline with its red word, the italic deck, a drop cap and columns, the plate, and the record in the margin.
sample:
The Saltmarsh Sheet

Autumn editionSaltmarsh Flower Market · a fictional marketPrice: free at the gate

The early-opening pilot

The Market Before Sunrise

Six Sundays of 5 a.m. flowers left the committee with 510 sales, 42 opinions and a $1,800 bill. Is that enough to keep the lights on early?

Before the first tram, before the bakeries lift their shutters, there is a particular smell at the Saltmarsh Flower Market: cold water, cut stems, diesel from the delivery vans. For six Sunday mornings this autumn, residents could walk into it. The market's pilot opened the stalls at 5 a.m. and closed them at 9, and the committee must now decide whether that window stays.

The committee did not set out to prove a point. It set out to learn whether anybody wanted flowers at that hour, and it paid for the lesson: $1,800 in additional staffing across the six weeks. The record below is what came back.

Fig. 1 · The window. 5 to 9 a.m. × six Sundays = 24 hours of early trading.

dos: Set the masthead once, in blackletter, between a double rule.
Run body in columns with hairline rules; open with a drop cap.
One red word per page; pull figures name their denominator.
Use engraved plates with Fig. captions; label invented scenes illustrative.
donts: No photographs; no colour fills larger than a tint box.
No rounded corners, shadows or gradients.
No blackletter anywhere but the masthead.
No percentage without its base in the same sentence.
binding_losses: The masthead face, the Franklin small-caps role, the column rules, the plate frame and the drop cap have no contract slot; they are bs-* classes. The contract names three families; Broadsheet uses four, so UnifrakturCook and Libre Franklin are set by class.
footer: Newsprint first, late edition second. Fonts: UnifrakturCook 700, Old Standard TT 400/700 and italic, Libre Franklin 400/500/600, Courier Prime 400/700, all Google-hosted.

hand.headline: An engraver’s line: hairlines, a line-screen for every tone.
hand.note: Broadsheet draws like a plate: 1.5px ink lines with square ends, and no flat tone anywhere. A filled region is a horizontal line-screen at a 4px pitch, in red for the one thing that matters and in ink for the rest; the quiet parts stay newsprint. Frame it, caption it with a Fig. number, mark it illustrative if it is.
rules: 1.5px ink, square caps. Hairlines, never heavy.
None. Tone is a horizontal line-screen, 4px pitch: red for the subject, ink for the rest.
The line-screen is the texture; the plate frame is the only ornament.
Old Standard bold for the one number; Franklin caps for the caption.
A plate may draw itself in on first view. Nothing else moves.

motion: Links take the red; nothing moves.
Buttons darken to newsprint-sunk. No transform.
None for text: the page is simply there. A plate may stroke-draw once on first view (reveal, 600ms); reduced motion shows it complete.
